channel.title: The Daily Plant
channel.description: An automatically generated daily podcast for the serious gardener and designer. Each episode is a focused, master-gardener-level deep dive on a single plant or genus relevant to the Eastern US — native species, the non-native ornamentals and invasives you encounter in real gardens — covering identification, range and ecology, culture, mature habit, design use, companions, and the best cultivars. Most episodes end with a short spaced-repetition quiz on plants covered earlier, to build lasting recall.

item.title: The Daily Plant — Bush-Honeysuckle (Diervilla)
item.description:
A deep dive on Diervilla, the native East Coast bush-honeysuckles, covering the three species and their ranges, the suckering habit that makes them a sleeper bank-stabilization shrub, the genus's outsized bumblebee value, and the Kodiak cultivar series with its unsettled hybrid parentage. item.title: The Daily Plant — Sassafras (Sassafras albidum)
item.description:
A deep dive on Sassafras albidum, the East Coast native tree carrying three leaf shapes on one plant and some of the best fall color in the region right now. Covers identification, the taproot and suckering habits that shape how you specify it, its two specialist moth and butterfly relationships, and laurel wilt disease — a current, spreading threat to Lauraceae that every Southeast and mid-Atlantic designer should be tracking. Closes with a four-plant recall quiz on Parthenocissus, Amelanchier, Carex, and Mitchella repens.

item.title: The Daily Plant — Euonymus: The Invasive Burning Bush and Its Native Cousin

A genus deep dive on the native shrubby Hypericums — prolificum, frondosum, densiflorum, and kalmianum — the East Coast's most underused midsummer-to-fall blooming shrub group. Covers the taxonomy that folded Ascyrum into Hypericum, buzz-pollination biology, culture and siting on real Eastern sites, disease pressure, and why the weedy European Hypericum perforatum gets confused with this garden-worthy genus. Closes with a recall quiz on Andropogon, Oxydendrum, Cephalanthus, Symphyotrichum, Silphium, and Franklinia.

item.title: The Daily Plant — Bluestem Grasses (Andropogon and Anatherum)
item.description:
A deep dive on the bluestem complex at the height of its late-summer bloom: Andropogon gerardii and Andropogon ternarius, the true bluestems, alongside their recently reclassified relatives Anatherum glomeratum and Anatherum virginicum, formerly lumped together as Andropogon. Covers the twenty twenty-three taxonomic split, culture and lodging risk, cultivars, and the rare Arogos skipper's dependence on big bluestem in coastal plain grasslands, closing with how to match each species to a site.

item.title: The Daily Plant — Franklin Tree (Franklinia alatamaha)
item.description:
A deep dive on Franklinia alatamaha, the Georgia native that has been extinct in the wild for two centuries and survives only as cultivated descendants of William Bartram's original seed collection. We cover the extinction mystery, the narrow cultural window that makes it a specimen rather than a workhorse, its late-summer-into-fall bloom that fills a real calendar gap, and how to weigh it against Stewartia pseudocamellia and Gordonia lasianthus in a design. Closes with a recall quiz on Pycnanthemum, Microstegium vimineum, and Chelone.

item.title: The Daily Plant — Japanese Stiltgrass (Microstegium vimineum)
item.description:
A deep dive on Microstegium vimineum, the shade-tolerant Asian annual grass now blanketing floodplains and forest understories up and down the East Coast. We cover the diagnostic silvery midrib, how to separate it from native whitegrass and basket grass, why its unusual shade-adapted physiology and deer-proof palatability make it such an effective invader, and the multi-year herbicide and hand-pulling strategy that actually works — with a note on why late summer is the critical action window.
